english_verification.review_scope: Translated the full article body before the National Ideas appendix and every non-national-ideas input pointer. Read the three cited Wiki chunks for representative historical and religious claims. Mission-tree mechanics are translated from the existing research, not exhaustively re-audited. The primary compared native idea names/descriptions with current English localisation keys (formatting codes stripped); original sources and optional sets are kept separate. Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Wiki's account of the dragon's lair and current sleep includes religious tradition and unconfirmed claims; the article preserves that qualification.
The source evidence notes no successor Tag; translated as remaining Z88 rather than a Tag change.
The referenced current-Mod history and representative mission ranges were checked, not every one of the 42 missions and event outcomes.

rationale.campaign_length: The requirement for three hundred battles, all Great Hunts, four hundred provinces following the same faith, and a place among the world's top three powers makes this a long campaign.
rationale.colonization: Colonisation of the northern frontier and Dalaire's coast is mandatory in the mission tree and is tied to the whale-oil industry.
rationale.complexity: Vassals, council seats, hunts, aerie capacity, development, colonisation, and battle counts all need to be planned together.
rationale.dark_story: Conflict and forced integration occur, but the main story emphasises cooperation, protection, and community rather than terror or extermination.
rationale.difficulty: There are many mechanical objectives and hard thresholds, but strong military rewards make the campaign broadly manageable once vassal management is familiar.
rationale.diplomacy: Old allies, protection, vassalisation, subject development, and council integration require long-term management of relations and liberty desire.
rationale.early_pressure: Its direct military strength is respectable, but multiple vassals' liberty desire, loans, or a regency can quickly disrupt the opening.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The white dragon, mage towers, and mithril give the setting a magical flavour, while the day-to-day campaign centres on military and institutional management.
rationale.narrative_density: 42 missions and numerous events tell a continuing story of exile, unification, hunts, the integration of diverse peoples, and an ending centred on the white dragon.
rationale.tall_play: Fifteen high-development provinces, the aerie, mage tower, forge, and mithril industry create clear development thresholds.
rationale.trade_economy: Ports, production, and whale oil form an economic strand, but are not the country's central standalone mechanic.
rationale.warfare: Northern unification, elite harpy troops, nine hunts, and the need to fight three hundred battles keep warfare central throughout.

identity.appearance: A 1444 starting harpy kingdom; the full mission chain remains Tag Z88 and does not form a successor country Tag.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
Centuries ago, our flight from the Moorhils and encroaching Alenic people forced us to flee north, across the frigid seas into the frozen lands of Gerudia. We found no new home but a warzone as our flock harassed by trollish attack. With nowhere left to flee, we faced certain death. By chance however, we were assisted in combat by a Gerudian warband from the east. In gratitude for this action, we vowed to assist the Gerudians in their efforts to reclaim the north from both the Trolls and Elkaesal cultists.

Our presence proved pivotal in the battles to come, as early scouting from the skies allowed our joint armies to outmanoeuvre any forces that opposed us. Further, we were able to rescue many injured warriors from certain death, bringing them back to the warcamps to rest and recover from their wounds. So crucial was our flock that even after the reclamation of Olavlund and Dalr was complete, our Gerudian allies continued to lean on us, starting a centuries old tradition. Even now, it is a not uncommon sight for battles along the Olavish coast to be watched by Járnklo Harpies, looking for those of heroic valour wounded in battle, to rescue them from certain death and bring them to recover in Vængheim.

description.text:
The Gerudian Frontier; a frigid and wild stretch of dense and frozen forest, full of riches to be claimed and danger to be bested. It is a land that many covet but few can justly claim. We are amongst those few. It was the Council of Skalds who granted us the right to the lands between the Titan’s Rest and Black Frost Mountains, our just reward for defeating the feared Skollm the Relentless.

That was centuries ago, in 621 AA. Since then we’ve taken roost in Djupfýri, the former heart of Skollm’s attacks and raids, and slowly expanded outward. Despite all this time, there is still much wealth waiting out in the frozen wastes - furs, gold and perhaps something more…

description.text:
Harpies have always been a people of song. Since the ancient days in old Bulwar, we have sung. Our ancestors cried out dirges mourning our first flight into Cannor after the fall of the first Firanyan Queendom. They shouted battle hymns marking our wars against the trolls. And they rang with ballads of how we found our home in the frozen north.

It is for this reason that when Elkaesal the White fell and the One Eyed Skald began teaching of the magical power of songs and saga to the peoples of Gerudia, for we were quick to take to his teachings.. We were amongst the first to adopt the burgeoning faith, amongst the first to preach about the pacification of Elkaesal through it, amongst the first to bring its capabilities to devastating effect in the field of battle. In doing so we developed a deep relationship with the council of Skalds. To this day there has always been at least one Harpy on the council to commemorate the ties between us.

description.text:
Harpies do not naturally do well in the bitter cold of Gerudia. Our wings, in particular, are often subject to extreme frostbite. And those who foolishly continue to fly often succumb to hypothermia brought on by the extreme blizzards and biting cold that this region presents.

However, we are not without solutions. By coating our wings with a layer of oils, we can protect ourselves from the worst of the effects of the freezing climate. This has, over time, developed into a strong industry on developing oil and oil-based products, with Vængheim being a centre of production of scented oils and candles for all of Cannor. Houses from Sornbay to Castonath have been warmed and comforted by the soft and gentle scents that our expertly crafted candles provide.

description.text:
Life along the Titan’s Rest is not easy, to say the least. We are constantly barraged with bitterly cold winds and snowstorms from the Blackfrost Mountains, and we were the worst hit by the Era of Black Ice, when the frigid winds hit a new low, causing many of the humans to the south to flee to warmer waters.

This reality, however, also provides us with a very useful advantage in the instance of war: our roost, which would already be difficult to lay siege to, is now known across the Giant’s Grave sea as impenetrable, as any attempt to scale it’s sheer cliff wall is exposed to the full and violent effects of the Gerudian weather. Many Dalric and Grombari soldiers have decayed and fallen to the joint assault of both our skilled warriors and the intense cold storms, and many shall yet in the future.

description.text:
The Battle-Maidens of Gerudia, the famous elite unit of warriors that acts as the core of the Vængheimer forces, formed in 584AA. Trained against the most elite of Reavers and warriors and forged in the fire of battle with the fearsome trolls of the north, they are experts in aerial harassment tactics, and can often inflict massive casualties on an attacking force with seeming ease.

Utilising the blinding snow-storms of their home region and lightning fast attack patterns of their past as raiders in prior flocks, their prowess and fearsomeness has been known across the Giant’s Grave battlefields for centuries. There is not much more terrifying to a warrior in Gerudia, than seeing this winged legion take flight against them.

description.text:
Due to our precarious position along the Gerudian Frontier, Vængheimer culture has developed a very militarist tendency. Many harpies and their husbands often maintain their own small forges, to repair their arms and armour privately. This allows for our army to be quickly raised in times of war, and quick to reinforce in case of casualties.

Growing in a home with a forge encourages many warriors to learn blacksmithing with a strong fervour, as the ability to repair your wares can literally mean your life and death. Later, during the era of artificery, many of the flock would turn to learning the skills required to augment and outfit their weapons and armour with various tools to assist in both their effectiveness in battle and maintenance.

player_overview.avoid_if: If you dislike extensive event text, vassal liberty desire, colonisation and hard development thresholds, or long-term planning for three hundred battles, this campaign may feel drawn out.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Early on, gather vassals, manage liberty desire, and unify Gerudia. In the midgame, alternate between council integration and Great Hunts while expanding. Later, build the aerie and mithril industry, colonise Dalaire, and complete the white-dragon and great-power objectives.
player_overview.overview: Vængheim is Cannor's distinctive harpy campaign in the north. Unify Gerudia through war, vassals, and a federal council, integrating trolls, humans, orcs, kobolds, and gnomes. Along the way, lead a chain of event-driven Great Hunts, build a tier-three aerie, forge mithril, and develop Dalaire's whale-oil industry across the sea. The ultimate goal is not a Tag change but Elkaesal the White's blessing and the defence of the north under Vængheim's own name.
player_overview.recommended_for: For players who enjoy northern epics, a multi-ethnic federation, vassal management, event-driven adventures, elite armies, and medium-to-long campaigns of expansion.
signature_features: A federal council uses limited seats to integrate several cultural groups and turn conquered peoples into represented members of the polity.
A Great Hunt event chain personally involving the ruler, with nine hunts and three hundred battles marking the progress of the legend.
Battlefield rescues unlock a tier-three aerie, supported by mithril forging, provincial development, and elite harpy armies.
player_overview.tagline: Lead Valkyrie-like harpies to unite the north, bring its peoples into one council, and make hunts, mithril, and the white dragon part of a new heroic saga.

reasons: 42 directly defined missions connect northern unification, a multiethnic federation, and the white dragon's mission into a complete heroic saga.
Great Hunts make the ruler's choices and adventure events a distinctive repeatable gameplay loop.
The federal council gives different conquered peoples their own narratives and permanent bonuses.
The tier-three aerie, mithril, and harpy armies create a clear military progression.
Development, colonisation, and warfare proceed together, giving the campaign a strong sense of stages.
warnings: Early vassal liberty desire and economic pressure can trigger a cascade of problems.
Three hundred battles, development thresholds, and Dalaire colonisation are significant hard requirements.
There is a large volume of event text; the most detailed community guide also uses several mods, so its values should not be copied over.

values.rationale: The multi-ethnic federal council, representation, civilian protection, and shared disaster response are strong institutional positives. Warfare and vassalisation reduce restraint, but do not undo the country's high recognition of personhood.
